title: blurb
Two centuries between seeing and believi: From animalcules in ditch water to penicillin by the gram — two centuries where you could watch contagion swim and the hospital still blamed bad air.

title: blood-circulation
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Spectacle glass bought a second scale; Harvey’s loop made the body a closed plumbing problem—fevers had to live *somewhere* in the circuit, not in the four humors.

title: microorganisms
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Stacked lenses were a toy until someone aimed them at ditch water: “animalcules” proved life at a scale physicians had no ward vocabulary for.

title: bacteria
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Smaller still, and named before anyone had a theory of disease—visibility without a job description.

title: smallpox-vaccine
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Empiricism runs ahead of theory: deliberate pus from a mild case stops the lethal one—Turkish practice, English controversy, no agreed germ in sight.

title: pathology
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Morgagni’s 640 autopsies make death legible organ by organ; the corpse table becomes evidence even while the living patient is still explained by bad air.

title: vaccination
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Jenner systematizes the trick—cowpox blisters as a manufactured shield—immunity without knowing what you are blocking.

title: anesthesia
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Ether buys painless cutting; operations multiply, and the wound you cannot feel becomes the new killer—surgery’s bottleneck shifts from pain to what walks in on the hands.

title: puerperal-fever
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Semmelweis counts bodies: the same doctor, different wards—contagion by contact, not miasma, years before anyone agrees on a microbe.

title: pasteurization
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Wine merchants pay for spoilage answers; heating kills what the lens already showed—biology as quality control before biology as bedside doctrine.

title: spontaneous-generation-rip
Two centuries between seeing and believi: The swan-neck flask kills “life from broth” on the bench; the open question moves from creation to *delivery*—germs ride dust, not vapor.

title: germ-theory-of-disease
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Pasteur gathers the threads: contagious disease has agents; medicine finally has something to hunt besides humors and smells.

title: antiseptic-surgery
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Lister weds phenol to Lister’s own problem—clean the cut, not just the air—anesthesia made the OR busy; antisepsis makes it survivable.

title: bacterial-cultivation
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Koch grows anthrax outside the body and pins one shape to one plague—identification becomes laboratory craft, not bedside argument.

title: anthrax-inoculation
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Jenner’s one-off becomes a recipe: attenuate in the lab when nature offers no mild cousin—manufactured weakness as armor.

title: rabies
Two centuries between seeing and believi: The same factory ships a bite protocol across species lines—rabies, not smallpox, is the public proof that the pipeline generalizes.

title: penicillin
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Fleming’s contaminated dish is a bench accident; the mold’s halo says some cells are killable without poisoning the patient—if anyone can purify it.

title: penicillin-practical
Two centuries between seeing and believi: Florey and Chain turn halo into grams; WWII demand finishes what germ theory started—mass death finally pays for mass production of cure.
